caddo-removal.description: Treaty of July 1, 1835, art. 2: the Caddo "promise to remove at their own expense out of the boundaries of the United States" within one year of signing, "and never more return". Art. 1 cedes all Caddo land in Louisiana and Arkansas.
caddo-removal.citation: Treaty with the Caddo, July 1, 1835, art. 2, 7 Stat. 470; 2 Kappler 432 (1904).
caddo-removal.quote: promise to remove at their own expense out of the boundaries of the United States and the territories belonging and appertaining thereto within the period of one year
caddo-removal.notes: The same article says the chiefs "do voluntarily relinquish" the land, so the treaty text itself presents the removal as agreed; the record below bears on how it was got.
caddo-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
caddo-removal.sentence: The Caddo promise to leave the United States at their own expense within one year and never return.
caddo-removal.source: Treaty with the Caddo, July 1, 1835, 7 Stat. 470

caddo-removal.description: The treaty is witnessed by "T. J. Harrison, captain, Third Regiment Infantry, commanding detachment": an army detachment was at the treaty ground.
caddo-removal.citation: Treaty with the Caddo, July 1, 1835, 7 Stat. 470 (witness list); 2 Kappler 432 (1904).
caddo-removal.quote: T. J. Harrison, captain, Third Regiment Infantry, commanding detachment
caddo-removal.notes: A detachment present at signing is not proof of coercion; it is noted because the 1841 testimony below refers to troops at the ground.
caddo-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
caddo-removal.sentence: Captain Harrison of the Third Infantry commands a detachment that witnesses the Caddo treaty.
caddo-removal.source: Treaty with the Caddo, July 1, 1835, 7 Stat. 470

caddo-removal.description: Testimony taken Dec. 1840 for the House: Joseph Valentin says he was on the ground at the 1835 treaty but "was sent off by Mr. Brooks, the commissioner, who told him that he was ordered by the Government to permit no one to be present but the interpreter".
caddo-removal.citation: Caddo Indian Treaty: Testimony Taken Under a Commission from the Committee on Indian Affairs, H.R. Doc. No. 25, 27th Cong., 2d Sess., at 8 (1841) (deposition of Joseph Valentin, Dec. 10, 1840).
caddo-removal.quote: was sent off by Mr. Brooks, the commissioner, who told him that he was ordered by the Government to permit no one to be present but the interpreter
caddo-removal.notes: Page approximate. The inquiry (Committee on Indian Affairs, 1840-41) concerned white claims to Rush Island land and Commissioner Jehiel Brooks's conduct, not the Caddo's removal as such; its witnesses are local whites and creoles. Valentin also says a man summoned by the Caddo to aid them was seized and another fled "from the troops".
caddo-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
caddo-removal.sentence: Joseph Valentin tells a House inquiry that Commissioner Brooks sent him off and allowed only the interpreter present.
caddo-removal.source: Caddo Indian Treaty: Testimony Taken Under a Commission from the Committee on Indian Affairs, H.R. Doc. No. 25, 27th Cong., 2d Sess. (1841)

caddo-removal.description: Valentin (same testimony): before the treaty the Caddo had already decided to leave for lands offered by the Mexican government, but "Their departure was arrested by Mr. Brooks, who told them that he had papers, and a gunsmith, and other things for them, and that he wished to buy their lands." The record shows the intent to leave existed before the treaty.
caddo-removal.citation: Caddo Indian Treaty: Testimony . . . , H.R. Doc. No. 25, 27th Cong., 2d Sess., at 16 (1841) (deposition of Joseph Valentin, Dec. 15, 1840).
caddo-removal.quote: Their departure was arrested by Mr. Brooks, who told them that he had papers, and a gunsmith, and other things for them, and that he wished to buy their lands.
caddo-removal.notes: Page approximate (the page marker "16 Doc. No. 25" falls just before this passage). Not a record of the move itself: no government report of the Caddo crossing into Texas in 1835-36 was found. The 1859 Texas removal is a separate journey (texas-reserves-removal).
caddo-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
caddo-removal.sentence: Valentin tells a House inquiry that Brooks halted the Caddo's plan to leave for land offered by Mexico.
caddo-removal.source: Caddo Indian Treaty: Testimony Taken Under a Commission from the Committee on Indian Affairs, H.R. Doc. No. 25, 27th Cong., 2d Sess. (1841)

texas-reserves-removal.description: Commissioner of Indian Affairs (J. W. Denver/A. B. Greenwood), June 11, 1859, to Superintendent Neighbors: authorized "to take measures forthwith for the removal of the Indians" from the Texas reserves to the country leased from the Choctaws and Chickasaws between 98 and 100 degrees west longitude, with a military escort requested from the Secretary of War.
texas-reserves-removal.citation: Office of Indian Affairs to R. S. Neighbors, June 11, 1859 (doc. no. 134), in Report of the Secretary of the Interior, S. Ex. Doc. No. 2, 36th Cong., 1st Sess. (Serial 1023), at 651 (1859).
texas-reserves-removal.quote: you are now authorized to take measures forthwith for the removal of the Indians to the section of country leased from the Choctaws and Chickasaws, and lying between the 98° and 100° of west longitude
texas-reserves-removal.notes: Order made conditional on the necessity continuing "at the date of the reception of these instructions". Page 651 from the running head in the text; the same letter says "The Secretary of War has been requested to furnish a strong military escort for your protection". The earlier decision to move the Indians "early in the fall or winter" is in the March 30, 1859 instructions (doc. no. 117), not fetched separately.
texas-reserves-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
texas-reserves-removal.sentence: The Indian Office authorizes Neighbors to remove the Native nations on the Texas reserves to land leased from the Choctaws and Chickasaws.
texas-reserves-removal.source: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, S. Ex. Doc. No. 2, 36th Cong., 1st Sess. (1859) (Serial 1023)

texas-reserves-removal.description: Commissioner to Superintendent Rector, June 15, 1859: Neighbors "has been directed, under date of June 11 . . . to proceed forthwith with the removal of the Texas Indians to the Wichita agency, under a strong escort of United States troops".
texas-reserves-removal.citation: Office of Indian Affairs to E. Rector, June 15, 1859 (doc. no. 135), in Report of the Secretary of the Interior, S. Ex. Doc. No. 2, 36th Cong., 1st Sess. (Serial 1023), at 652 (1859).
texas-reserves-removal.quote: to proceed forthwith with the removal of the Texas Indians to the Wichita agency, under a strong escort of United States troops for his protection
texas-reserves-removal.notes: Page approximate (652). Orders to the army: the Secretary of War furnished the escort (Maj. George H. Thomas, 2d Cav., and infantry).
texas-reserves-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
texas-reserves-removal.sentence: The Indian Office orders Rector to proceed with the removal under a strong escort of United States troops.
texas-reserves-removal.source: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, S. Ex. Doc. No. 2, 36th Cong., 1st Sess. (1859) (Serial 1023)

texas-reserves-removal.description: Neighbors, Aug. 18, 1859, from the Washita: he left the Brazos agency on Aug. 1, the Comanches left on July 30 under Capt. Gilbert; the combined escort was one infantry company and two companies of 2d Cavalry under Maj. G. H. Thomas; they crossed Red River Aug. 8 and reached the False Washita on the 16th.
texas-reserves-removal.citation: R. S. Neighbors to Commissioner of Indian Affairs, Aug. 18, 1859 (doc. no. 162), in Report of the Secretary of the Interior, S. Ex. Doc. No. 2, 36th Cong., 1st Sess. (Serial 1023), at 696-97 (1859).
texas-reserves-removal.quote: Our escort consisted of one company of infantry and two companies of second cavalry, all under the command of Major G. H. Thomas.
texas-reserves-removal.numbers: about 1,050 from the lower (Brazos) reserve and 380 from the upper (Comanche) reserve, per Neighbors July 25 (doc. no. 161a); 1,415 colonized, per the Commissioner
texas-reserves-removal.deaths: none recorded in these letters; Neighbors was murdered on his way back to Texas in Sept. 1859 (Special Agent Leeper's letter of Sept. 15 reports it)
texas-reserves-removal.dates: Aug. 1 - Aug. 16, 1859; turned over to Agent Blain Sept. 1, 1859
texas-reserves-removal.notes: The sentence quoted is on p. 697 (after the running head). The earlier sentence ("I left Brazos agency, Texas, with Indians of that reserve, on the 1st instant") is split by the page header, so it is not quoted. Neighbors says he sold the Indians' hogs and left the houses behind.
texas-reserves-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
texas-reserves-removal.sentence: Neighbors reports that his escort is one infantry company and two cavalry companies under Major Thomas.
texas-reserves-removal.source: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, S. Ex. Doc. No. 2, 36th Cong., 1st Sess. (1859) (Serial 1023)

texas-reserves-removal.description: Neighbors, July 25, 1859, on the eve of the march: "I shall leave within the next four days with about 1,050 Indians from this reserve, and 380 from the upper reserve."
texas-reserves-removal.citation: R. S. Neighbors to E. Rector, July 25, 1859 (doc. no. 161a), in Report of the Secretary of the Interior, S. Ex. Doc. No. 2, 36th Cong., 1st Sess. (Serial 1023), at 696 (1859).
texas-reserves-removal.quote: I shall leave within the next four days with about 1,050 Indians from this reserve, and 380 from the upper reserve.

ponca-removal.quote: whether by force or otherwise does not appear
ponca-removal.notes: IMPORTANT for accuracy: the opinion does NOT find that the 1877 removal was forced. Full sentence: "The Poncas lived upon their reservation in southern Dakota ... until two or three years ago, when they removed therefrom, but whether by force or otherwise does not appear." Use the opinion for (a) the military arrest of Standing Bear's party in 1879 and (b) the holding at 701, ¶ 3: "no rightful authority exists for removing by force any of the relators to the Indian Territory". Court also notes the 1868 treaty extinguished their reserve "without consultation with, or knowledge or consent on the part of, the Ponca tribe" (at 698).

rogue-river-removal.description: Palmer: about 600 at Port Orford and 250 at the mouth of the Rogue 'unconditionally surrendered' and 'will be escorted to the southern part of the coast reservation by United States troops'.
rogue-river-removal.citation: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, in Message from the President, H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 1, 34th Cong., 3d Sess., at 763 (1856) (Palmer, June 23, 1856)
rogue-river-removal.quote: They will be escorted to the southern part of the coast reservation by United States troops, together with any of the other bands that may come in.

rogue-river-removal.sentence: Palmer reports that about 850 Native people surrender unconditionally and will be escorted to the coast reservation by United States troops.
rogue-river-removal.source: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, in Message from the President, H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 1, 34th Cong., 3d Sess. (1856)

rogue-river-removal.description: Palmer, June 23, 1856: all the hostile bands had come in and 'unconditionally surrendered themselves as prisoners of war'.
rogue-river-removal.citation: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, in Message from the President, H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 1, 34th Cong., 3d Sess., at 762 (1856) (Palmer, June 23, 1856)
rogue-river-removal.quote: have come in, and unconditionally surrendered themselves as prisoners of war.
rogue-river-removal.notes: Fragment of a longer sentence ('All the hostile bands, with the exception of Johns . . . have come in, and unconditionally surrendered themselves as prisoners of war').
rogue-river-removal.checked: matched by script against the fetched text (Nov. 27, 2026)
rogue-river-removal.sentence: Palmer reports that the hostile bands have come in and surrendered unconditionally as prisoners of war.
rogue-river-removal.source: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, in Message from the President, H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 1, 34th Cong., 3d Sess. (1856)

rogue-river-removal.description: Palmer's July 3, 1856 report: Colonel Buchanan's terms, relayed to Chief John's sons, were to 'come and go to the coast reservation under an escort of United States troops'; 421 Indians joined Captain Augur's camp, making 708 who marched to Port Orford.
rogue-river-removal.citation: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, in Message from the President, H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 1, 34th Cong., 3d Sess., at 768 (1856) (Palmer, July 3, 1856, doc. no. 92)
rogue-river-removal.quote: the conditions offered by Colonel Buchanan, and explaining to them the advantage likely to accrue'to the tribe by yielding to the terms; which were, to come and go to the coast reservation under an escort of United States troops.
rogue-river-removal.numbers: 708 on the march to Port Orford (about May-June 1856)
rogue-river-removal.notes: Quote contains the scan's apostrophe glitch ('accrue'to'). Page 768 inferred from page markers (769 follows).

rogue-river-removal.sentence: Palmer reports that Colonel Buchanan offers Chief John's sons terms to come and go to the coast reservation under an escort of troops.
rogue-river-removal.source: Report of the Secretary of the Interior, in Message from the President, H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 1, 34th Cong., 3d Sess. (1856)

rogue-river-removal.description: Wool, June 3, 1856: the Rogue River Indians 'are surrendering themselves unconditionally, and will be conducted to the coast reservation as soon as collected together'.
rogue-river-removal.citation: H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 118, 34th Cong., 1st Sess., at 54 (1856) (Wool, June 3, 1856)
rogue-river-removal.quote: The Indians are surrender¬ ing themselves unconditionally, and will be conducted to the coast reservation as soon as collected together.

rogue-river-removal.sentence: General Wool reports that the Rogue River people are surrendering unconditionally and will be taken to the coast reservation.
rogue-river-removal.source: H.R. Ex. Doc. No. 118, 34th Cong., 1st Sess. (1856)

rogue-river-removal.description: Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde, History and Culture page; it speaks of the forced removal of tribal members from ancestral lands (link only; not quoted).
rogue-river-removal.citation: Confederated Tribes of the Grand Ronde Community of Oregon, History, https://www.grandronde.org/history-culture/history/
rogue-river-removal.notes: Loads (200). Siletz: https://www.ctsi.nsn.us/ (returned 403 to a script; a person should check).

rogue-river-removal.description: Grand Ronde agent's 1857 report on the Umpqua and Calapooia bands (a neighbouring group moved at the same time): on the outbreak of the Rogue River war they were 'hurried away' to the reservation without time to sell their effects, and many died of sickness.
rogue-river-removal.citation: Annual Report of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs for the Year 1857, at 363 (Gov't Printing Off. 1858) (Grande Ronde agency report, July 21, 1857)
rogue-river-removal.quote: they were consequently hurried away without giving them time either to remove or sell their effects
rogue-river-removal.notes: About the Umpqua/Calapooia bands, not the Rogue River bands themselves; the same report (p. 362) says the Rogue River and Shasta majority were moved to Siletz. Palmer's ARCIA 1856 letters are the same ones cited from the H.R. Ex. Doc. 1 volume.

rogue-river-removal.sentence: The Grand Ronde agent reports that the Umpqua and Calapooia bands are hurried away without time to sell their effects.
